extra_misconceptions.fact: Nonwoven fabrics like felt and medical masks bond fibers directly together using heat, chemicals, or mechanical entanglement.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every textile product must be woven or knitted from spun yarn to be classified as a true fabric.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Fibers are the individual hair-like units that are twisted into yarn, which is then interlaced or bonded to form a finished fabric.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The terms fiber, yarn, and fabric mean the exact same thing in textile engineering and manufacturing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Industrial technical textiles reinforce automobile tires, filter municipal water, and form heat shields on spacecraft.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Textiles are only used for clothing, bedding, and household upholstery rather than heavy industrial engineering.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Manufactured fibers extruded from petrochemicals, wood pulp, and molten glass make up a large share of modern everyday textiles.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: All fibers used to make everyday fabrics come exclusively from agricultural plants or sheared farm animals.

extra_socratic_questions: What structural change turns raw loose fibers into a usable yarn before it becomes a woven or knitted fabric?
Which physical indicator shows whether an everyday item like a seat belt or surgical mask qualifies as a textile?
Under what condition does a collection of raw fibers qualify as a nonwoven fabric without being spun into yarn?
Why is it dangerous to wear loose, untreated cotton clothing instead of flame-resistant textiles near an open campfire?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rayon and lyocell are manufactured cellulosic fibers because wood pulp must be chemically dissolved and extruded through a spinneret.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rayon and lyocell are natural plant fibers because their raw material originates from harvested trees and bamboo.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Requirement 2a specifies 100% unblended swatches so you can observe the distinct traits of each individual fiber class.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A 50/50 cotton-polyester blend shirt satisfies the swatch requirement for a pure natural or synthetic sample.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most synthetic fibers are hydrophobic and absorb very little water, which helps them dry quickly but can trap body sweat.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Synthetic fibers like nylon and polyester absorb more moisture into their core than natural cotton or wool.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Silk is a natural protein fiber extruded by silkworm larvae when they spin protective cocoons during metamorphosis.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Silk is a plant-based cellulosic fiber harvested from tropical seed pods in the same manner as cotton.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a synthetic polyester swatch compared to a 100% cotton swatch when exposed to high heat?
Which physical indicator on a garment care label confirms that a swatch is a pure fiber rather than a blended fabric?
Why is rayon classified as a manufactured cellulosic fiber even though it starts from natural wood pulp?
What happens to the insulating ability of wool versus cotton when a hiker's base layer gets soaked in cold rain?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Woven fabrics interlace perpendicular warp and weft yarns, whereas knitted fabrics form interlocking loops that stretch easily.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Knitted fabrics are constructed by crisscrossing two perpendicular sets of straight yarns over and under each other.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Only animal hair fibers like wool have microscopic overlapping scales that ratchet together during wet felting agitation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Acrylic and polyester yarns will felt and shrink into a solid mat just like 100% animal wool in hot soapy water.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most natural dyes wash out of cellulose fibers rapidly unless the fabric is pre-treated with a mineral mordant like alum or iron.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Natural plant dyes from berries or onion skins bond permanently to cotton fibers without needing a mordant.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Water-repellent finishes cause droplets to bead while leaving pores breathable, whereas waterproof coatings seal pores completely.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Waterproofed canvas and water-repellent fabrics block liquid water using the exact same pore-sealing coating.

extra_socratic_questions: Which visual pattern under a magnifying glass distinguishes a knitted fabric from a plain woven or nonwoven sample?
What happens to the width of a handwoven belt on a simple cardboard loom if you pull the weft yarn too tight on each pass?
Why is it dangerous to boil natural dye baths or apply waterproofing chemicals in unventilated indoor spaces or food pots?
What microscopic surface structure on wool fibers allows hot water and agitation to lock them into a dense felt sheet?

extra_misconceptions.fact: In weaving, the shed is the temporary V-shaped opening between raised and lowered warp threads through which the weft passes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The shed on a weaving loom refers to the storage room where raw cotton bales and wooden spindles are kept dry.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Aramid fibers provide heat and ballistic protection, while carbon fibers offer rigid, high-strength reinforcement for aerospace parts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Aramid and carbon fibers are stretchy elastomers used alongside spandex in athletic compression shorts.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Greige goods are freshly woven or knitted fabrics straight off the loom that have not yet been bleached, dyed, or finished.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Greige goods are defective fabrics that have turned gray from mildew damage during ocean shipping.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most natural fibers except silk grow in short staple lengths, while extruded synthetic filaments are often cut into staple for blending.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: All natural fibers come in continuous filaments, whereas all manufactured fibers are produced only in short staple lengths.

extra_socratic_questions: What mechanical role do the harness and heddles play in opening a shed for the shuttle to pass through on a loom?
Which processing step separates a soft carded sliver from a finished worsted yarn ready for weaving suiting fabric?
What happens to a polymer solution as it is forced through the tiny holes of a spinneret during synthetic fiber extrusion?
Why do textile mills inspect and test greige goods before investing energy and chemicals into bleaching, dyeing, or printing?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Conventional cotton cultivation requires large volumes of irrigation water, synthetic fertilizers, and agricultural pesticides.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Natural plant fibers like conventional cotton have zero environmental footprint because they are biodegradable crops.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Synthetic textiles shed thousands of microscopic plastic fibers into wastewater during every routine household laundry cycle.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Synthetic garments only pollute the environment when they are discarded into municipal landfills at the end of their use.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Repeated consumer washing in hot water and high-heat tumble drying often consume more total energy than initial fabric manufacturing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Manufacturing factory production accounts for nearly all of the energy consumed over a textile garment's life cycle.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Intimately blended natural and synthetic fibers are difficult to separate chemically or mechanically during textile recycling.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Blended fabrics like poly-cotton are the easiest textiles to recycle into new high-grade clothing fibers.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to synthetic fleece garments in a home washing machine that creates an ecological hazard in waterways?
Which resource trade-off must you weigh when comparing irrigation-heavy cotton farming against petroleum-based polyester?
Under what condition does manufacturing cellulosic rayon cause severe chemical pollution despite using renewable wood pulp?
What changes in consumer laundry habits reduce the largest share of energy consumption across a garment's life cycle?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The modern textile sector employs polymer chemists, biomedical engineers, automated loom programmers, and supply chain analysts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Careers in the textile industry are limited to low-skill sewing machine operation and retail clothing sales.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Automated weaving technicians and dyeing machinery specialists often train through community colleges and paid manufacturer apprenticeships.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every high-paying technical position in a modern textile plant requires a four-year university engineering degree.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Apparel and textile designers must evaluate drape, tensile strength, colorfastness, and care requirements so garments perform in use.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Fashion designers select fabric aesthetics without needing to understand fiber chemistry, weave structure, or shrinkage.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Domestic textile mills and universities lead global research in nonwoven medical fabrics, aerospace composites, and smart e-textiles.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The United States textile industry has completely vanished and no longer conducts research or manufacturing.

extra_socratic_questions: Which daily engineering duties separate a textile chemical colorist from a mechanical loom maintenance technician?
What laboratory tests would a textile quality assurance engineer run before approving fabric for firefighter turnout gear?
Where do polymer chemists and industrial designers collaborate when developing a new moisture-wicking athletic fabric?
What financial and career factors should you compare between a technical apprenticeship and a four-year textile degree?
